To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

amplifications within a regulatory repeat in intronic egfr are associated not only with the expression of EGFR and its ligands but also with caveolin-1 (involved in endocytosis) and eps15 (involved in EGFR signalling).
amplification of egfr in phyllodes is associated with the over-expression of the caveolin-1 receptor, the EGF receptor, pAkt, and pERK.
egfr amplifications are associated with the regulation of eps15 and the expression of caveol-1, which in turn are involved in the turnover and signalling of EGFR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of breast phyllode tumours, a rare tumour entity of the female breast, which is often misdiagnosed as breast cancer.
the identification of the molecular pathways that are responsible for the initiation and progression from a benign phyllodes tumour to a sarcomatous phyllodes tumou.
the identification of molecular pathways that are involved in carcinogenesis of phyllodes tumors of the breast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
amplification of the egfr CA- SSRI is associated with the up-regulation of caveolin- 1, eps15 and EGF, and with the down-regulation of TGF-α.

amplification of the egfr gene in phyllodes is associated with the overexpression of a number of proteins involved in the regulation of EGFR turnover and signal transduction, which is in line with the hypothesis of a major role of the EGFR signalling pathway in the initiation and progression in phyllodes breast tumours.
the presence of CA-SSR-I amplifications is associated with the expression and regulation of a number of proteins involved in the turnover and signalling of the EGFR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
amplifications of egfr in phyllodes are associated with a deregulation of genes involved in the turnover and signalling of EGFR.
egfr amplifications are associated with a specific gene expression pattern and that these amplifications may be a useful diagnostic marker in phyllodes tumors.
egfr amplifications in phylloids are associated with the activation of the epidermis growth factor pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
amplifications of egfr are not only associated with the expression and signalling of EGFR but also of caveolin- 1 and eps15.

the presence of amplifications within the regulatory egfr gene is associated with a specific gene expression pattern in phyllodes breast tumours, and the expression of caveolins and eps15 is correlated with the expression levels of EGFR, pERK and pAkt.
